rows.label: S — Scope first
rows.value: Read scope document completely. Extract: in-scope assets, exclusions, authorised techniques, RoE, emergency contacts, timeline. Write a one-page reconnaissance plan before opening any tool.

rows.label: C — Collect passively
rows.value: WHOIS → DNS (all 8 record types + subdomain enum) → Search engine (Google Dorks + robots.txt + sitemap.xml) → OSINT (Shodan, Wayback Machine, GitHub, LinkedIn). In that sequence. Zero contact with target systems.

rows.label: O — Organise findings
rows.value: Document every finding at moment of discovery: source, evidence (screenshot/text), severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), recommended action. The report is built continuously — not retrospectively.

rows.label: U — Understand attack surface
rows.value: Build the attack surface map. Prioritise: Critical (active exposure) → High (direct attack paths) → Medium (requires more work) → Low (background intelligence). This map guides active testing.

rows.label: T — Tell immediately
rows.value: Critical findings (live data exposure, active breach indicators, production backups publicly accessible) go to client emergency contact NOW — not in the final report. Document the notification in the engagement log.

rows.label: Step 1 — Registration
rows.value: WHOIS: registrar, registration date, nameservers, privacy status. Validate: does this domain actually belong to the client? Registration date indicates infrastructure age.

rows.label: Step 2 — DNS (all 8 types)
rows.value: A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME, PTR, SRV. Add every discovered subdomain to investigation queue. Note: CDN IPs vs direct IPs (CDN gap). DMARC p= value. Service verification tokens in TXT.

rows.label: Step 3 — Subdomain enum
rows.value: crt.sh (Certificate Transparency — passive). Wordlist brute force (active — confirm RoE). Zone transfer attempt on self-managed NS (active — confirm RoE). Repeat steps 1–2 on each discovered subdomain.

rows.label: Step 4 — Search engine recon
rows.value: site:domain.com (footprint). filetype:pdf/xlsx/docx/env (documents). intitle:"index of" (directories). inurl:admin/login/portal (portals). robots.txt + sitemap.xml. Wayback Machine. GitHub + Pastebin. Shodan (org:, ssl:, hostname:).

rows.label: Step 5 — Document metadata
rows.value: ExifTool on any discovered documents. Author, organisation, software version, embedded file paths, revision dates.

rows.label: CRITICAL — escalate immediately
rows.value: Unauthenticated endpoints returning live data. Open directories with production backups. Active credentials in passive sources. Active attacker activity. Active phishing targeting client's customers.

rows.label: HIGH — first active testing priority
rows.value: Dev/legacy servers with direct IPs (no CDN). Admin portals publicly accessible. DMARC p=none (domain spoofable). Exposed internal documents. Legacy systems on direct IP.

rows.label: MEDIUM — active testing, normal priority
rows.value: CDN-protected main application. Subdomains with unknown software versions. Cloud vendor disclosures. Document metadata findings. Portals with unknown versions.

rows.label: LOW — documented, low priority
rows.value: Standard registration data. Email provider identification. Technology stack inference from job postings (unconfirmed). Historical Wayback Machine data.

rows.label: 1. Asset Inventory
rows.value: Complete list of domains, subdomains, IPs attributed to target. In-scope vs discovered-but-not-in-scope. Source for each asset.

rows.label: 2. Infrastructure Architecture
rows.value: CDN-protected vs direct-IP assets. Hosting providers. CDN gap. Relationships between assets. Single points of failure (e.g., DNS account control).

rows.label: 3. Technology Stack
rows.value: Email platform (MX). CRM/SaaS (TXT tokens). CDN (NS/CNAME). Hosting (IP WHOIS). Software versions (Shodan, metadata, cached pages). Multi-source vs single-source confirmed.

rows.label: 4. Email Security Posture
rows.value: SPF: authorised senders, enforcement level (~all / -all). DMARC: p= value, rua reporting address. DKIM: confirmed or unconfirmed. Overall spoofability assessment.

rows.label: 5. Critical Findings
rows.value: Each critical and high finding with: discovery method, URL, evidence type, severity, status (active/remediated), recommended action.

rows.label: Scope first, always
rows.value: Read scope document completely before any information gathering. Confirm every action against RoE before performing it.

rows.label: Minimum necessary access
rows.value: Prove the exposure exists. Do not read, download, or use content beyond what the proof requires.

rows.label: Immediate escalation
rows.value: Critical findings go to client emergency contact during the engagement. Not in the final report. Not at report-out.

rows.label: Source every finding
rows.value: Query / tool / date / result / screenshot. Every finding. No exceptions. An unsourced finding is not a professional finding.

rows.label: Diminishing returns test
rows.value: Two consecutive hours of passive recon with no new finding categories = passive recon at completion. The attack surface map is actionable when this test is met.
